normalized.description: Objective: To develop a bi-directional DC/DC converter able to charge and discharge a generic storage system with a targeted reduction of 50% area and mass in the charge/discharge system.Description: Most of the current state of the art considers a dedicated converter for charging and a dedicated converter for discharging power into and from the energy storage system. This has impacts on the overall area and mass, as just half of the circuitry is in use at a given time. For those missions where mass and volume is a concern, a bi-directional converter allows to increase the power density and therefore to minimize mass and volume. In addition, currently the solution to charge and discharge an energy storage system is specific to the energy storage system in use. This activity aims to develop a bi-directional charge and discharge module, allowing the same circuitry to be used for charging and for discharging. The benefit of the bi-directionality reduces the area and the mass of the HW by 50%. On top, it is intended to analyze a generic solution to cover different energy storage systems (e.g. Li-Ion batteries and RFCS -Regenerative Fuel Cell Systems-). This provides a lot of flexibility, since the HW of the power management subsystem does not depend on the energy storage system, and therefore could be produced in advance. This also could lead to a reduction in time to delivery by 30%, by allowing recurrent use of the same design. The objective is challenging because the behavior of these storage systems is quite different and the converter must adapt to them. A charger/discharge module with bi-directional capability based on a non-isolated DC/DC topology with new switching devices (e.g.GaN based switches) and a versatile control system to adapt to the different storage systems. Possibly digital control may be considered to perform an adequate management of the battery or RFCS. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Confirmation of the scope of the charger/discharge (energy storage systems to be compatible with, power levels...) with a final consolidation of the preliminary requirements - Identify potential solutions (best topologies, control logic, switching devices...) and perform dedicated trade-offs to select a baseline - Design of the baseline, with the appropriate design analysis - Prototype manufacturing of a bi-directional charge and discharge module - Testing of a prototype - Analyse test results, identify and check deviations, implement corrections on the prototype if any to cover deviations to a final designDeliverables: Breadboard, Report
